AcceptedOut.description:
The deliberately uninformative answer to "did that address exist?".

docs/11's threat model: `/auth/request-otp` and `/auth/forgot-password` answer identically for
a known and an unknown address, or they are a membership oracle.
AcceptedOut.title: AcceptedOut

CellOut.description:
One number with the context that makes it mean something.

``percentile`` is docs/08 §"Instrument factsheet"'s improvement over the reference product:
"a small bar behind each cell showing that value's percentile within the current universe".
``null`` where the value is null — an unknown number has no rank.
CellOut.title: CellOut

ChangePasswordIn.description: ``current_password`` is optional: an OTP-only account is *setting* one for the first time.
ChangePasswordIn.title: ChangePasswordIn

CheckoutSessionOut.description:
docs/07: "-> Razorpay order/subscription payload".

Exactly what Razorpay's browser widget needs, and nothing that identifies another account.
`key_id` is the *publishable* key; the secret never leaves the service.
CheckoutSessionOut.title: CheckoutSessionOut

CircuitsFilter.description:
Maximum permitted circuit-hit days in the window. ``> 250`` means ignore (docs/01 §2.6).

Note the asymmetry with the other sentinels: the ignore value is a *threshold*, not a single
magic number, because any cap above a full year of trading days cannot bind.
CircuitsFilter.title: CircuitsFilter

ColumnOut.description: docs/07: "the 34 selectable result columns" — docs/01 §4 in fact enumerates 36.
ColumnOut.title: ColumnOut

DataExportOut.description:
docs/11 §Compliance: "DPDP Act: ... **data export** and deletion endpoints".

Everything the account owns, in one JSON document. `screens` and `consents` are lists of
objects rather than typed models because their shapes are already defined elsewhere and a
second copy here would be a second thing to keep in step.
DataExportOut.title: DataExportOut

DeleteAccountIn.description: Deleting is irreversible after the window, so it asks for the address back.
DeleteAccountIn.title: DeleteAccountIn

ExtraFactor.description: Factor two / factor three of the combined ranking (docs/01 §2.12).
ExtraFactor.title: ExtraFactor

FactorOut.description: docs/07: "factor registry (key, label, family, unit, higher_is_better)".
FactorOut.title: FactorOut

FactsheetOut.description: docs/07: "Factsheet payload mirrors the teardown §5 exactly".
FactsheetOut.title: FactsheetOut

GaugeOut.description: One of docs/01 §6's four breadth gauges.
GaugeOut.title: GaugeOut

IndexRowOut.description:
One row of docs/01 §7's ~145-index dashboard.

"each: name, % change, level, absolute change, PE, PB, Div Yield ... Includes derived indices
with no fundamentals (`Nifty50 PR 1x Inverse`, `India VIX`) → PE/PB/DivYield shown as `-`."

`null`, not `0`, for a missing fundamental — the em dash is the UI's rendering of the absence,
and a zero would be a claim that the index has a P/E of nought.
IndexRowOut.title: IndexRowOut

InstrumentHeaderOut.description:
docs/01 §5 block 1 — "symbol, ₹ price, full name, `NSE: SYMBOL`, index membership chips".

Two prices, because they answer different questions: `close_raw` is the exchange print the
header shows, `close` is the adjusted series every factor on the page was computed from
(CLAUDE.md house rule 6). Series, Listed On and Face Value are *not* here — docs/01 §5 puts
them in blocks 2 and 5, and duplicating them would be two places to drift.
InstrumentHeaderOut.title: InstrumentHeaderOut

InvoiceOut.description:
One row of `GET /invoices` — docs/07 §"Account & billing".

Every amount is a string-exact `Decimal`, and the tax is broken out per head because that is
what the customer's own accountant needs (docs/11 §Compliance).
InvoiceOut.title: InvoiceOut

ListingOut.description: One row of the listings register — an `instrument`, not a table of its own.
ListingOut.title: ListingOut

MarketHealthHistoryOut.description:
docs/07: `GET /market-health/history?universe=&from=&to=`.

"The four series for charting", plus the overlay docs/08 §"Market Health" asks for.
MarketHealthHistoryOut.title: MarketHealthHistoryOut

MarketHealthOut.description: docs/01 §6 — `Market Health — <universe>` and its four gauges.
MarketHealthOut.title: MarketHealthOut

MarketHealthPointOut.description: One day of the four series, with the universe's own index level for the overlay.
MarketHealthPointOut.title: MarketHealthPointOut

MarketQualityOut.description: docs/01 §5 block 10, with docs/05 §15's two distances beside the label.
MarketQualityOut.title: MarketQualityOut

MetricCardOut.description: docs/01 §5 block 4 — "value, sparkline, and a subdued `Median: x` line".
MetricCardOut.title: MetricCardOut

PeFilter-Input.description: P/E band behind its own switch. Undefined P/E is excluded when on (docs/01 §2.8).
PeFilter-Input.title: PeFilter

PeFilter-Output.description: P/E band behind its own switch. Undefined P/E is excluded when on (docs/01 §2.8).
PeFilter-Output.title: PeFilter

PlanFeatureOut.description:
One line of "what you get", as the plan row records it.

``entitlement`` is ``None`` for the two docs/01 §1 features this service cannot enforce —
community Slack and the AMAs — so the UI can render them without pretending they are gated.
PlanFeatureOut.title: PlanFeatureOut

PlanListOut.description: The catalogue plus everything the checkout page is legally required to show.
PlanListOut.title: PlanListOut

PlanOut.description:
docs/07: `GET /plans`. Everything `/pricing` renders comes from here.

PROMPTS.md Prompt 13 acceptance criterion 4: "No price or entitlement is hard-coded in the web
app; all read from the API." So the price, the label, the tagline, the feature list, the
Dec-2026 price and the Forever disclosure are all fields, not copy in a component.
PlanOut.title: PlanOut

PositiveDaysFilter.description: Minimum % of trading days that closed up. ``0`` means ignore (docs/01 §2.5).
PositiveDaysFilter.title: PositiveDaysFilter

ProblemOut.description: RFC 9457. ``extra="allow"`` carries the per-type members docs/07 attaches.
ProblemOut.title: ProblemOut

RangeFilter-Input.description: An inclusive ``[from, to]`` band; both ``None`` means ignore (docs/06 step 4).
RangeFilter-Input.title: RangeFilter

RangeFilter-Output.description: An inclusive ``[from, to]`` band; both ``None`` means ignore (docs/06 step 4).
RangeFilter-Output.title: RangeFilter

RankHistoryOut.description: docs/07: "this stock's rank over time in a screen".
RankHistoryOut.title: RankHistoryOut

RegisterIn.description:
docs/07: `POST /auth/register`.

``password`` is optional because docs/11 §Security makes OTP "the default path, password
optional" — an account created without one signs in by code until it sets one.
RegisterIn.title: RegisterIn

ScreenDefinition-Input.description:
The persisted screen configuration.

Two definitions that mean the same thing produce the same :meth:`canonical_json`, and
therefore the same :meth:`definition_hash` — which is what makes the Redis cache key
(docs/06 §Caching) and ``screen_run.definition_hash`` trustworthy.
ScreenDefinition-Input.title: ScreenDefinition

ScreenDefinition-Output.description:
The persisted screen configuration.

Two definitions that mean the same thing produce the same :meth:`canonical_json`, and
therefore the same :meth:`definition_hash` — which is what makes the Redis cache key
(docs/06 §Caching) and ``screen_run.definition_hash`` trustworthy.
ScreenDefinition-Output.title: ScreenDefinition

ScreenRunResponse.description: docs/07 §"Running a screen", field for field.
ScreenRunResponse.title: ScreenRunResponse

ScreenRunRowOut.description:
One result row: ``rank`` plus one member per entry of ``columns``.

``extra="allow"`` because the column set is the user's, not the schema's — which is what
docs/01 §4's column picker means. In OpenAPI this becomes ``additionalProperties``, so the
generated client types the known keys and permits the rest.
ScreenRunRowOut.title: ScreenRunRowOut

SessionOut.description:
What a successful authentication returns.

The refresh token is **not** here — it goes out as an httpOnly cookie and nowhere else
(docs/11 §Security). A response body that also carried it would put a 30-day credential
somewhere JavaScript can read.
SessionOut.title: SessionOut

TopRiskFilter.description: "Ignore Top Beta / Top Volatility" — a precomputed per-universe flag (docs/06 step 4).
TopRiskFilter.title: TopRiskFilter

TradingDaysOut.description: docs/07: "list of trading dates (for the historical date picker)".
TradingDaysOut.title: TradingDaysOut

WebhookAck.description:
What Razorpay is told. Deliberately uninformative: a delivery is acknowledged or retried,
and telling an unauthenticated caller which account an event touched would be a leak.
WebhookAck.title: WebhookAck

get.description:
docs/07: "this stock's rank over time in a screen".

Read from ``screen_run.results``, which docs/04 defines as "[{rank, instrument_id,
factor_value}]" — the audit trail of what the screen actually returned on each date. It is
*not* recomputed: the point of a rank history is what the screen said at the time, and
re-running today's engine over past data would answer a different question.

That also means the series is only as long as the screen's run history. A screen run once has
one point, and the response says so rather than padding it.
